title: Quizzer AI
description: An AI-powered adaptive learning platform that generates unlimited, tailored programming quizzes using Google Gemini. Features a 3-step generative pipeline, context-aware explanations, and a gamified progression system built on a Service-Oriented Django architecture.
longDescription:
Quizzer AI replaces static question banks with dynamically generated programming quizzes powered by the Google Gemini API. A custom 3-step AI pipeline handles intent parsing from natural language prompts, structured quiz generation with strict JSON enforcement, and targeted mistake analysis that provides context-aware explanations for incorrect answers.

Built on a Service-Oriented Django backend with HTMX and Alpine.js on the frontend, the platform delivers SPA-like interactivity without a separate JavaScript framework. It includes a full gamification system with XP progression, leveling, daily streaks, and 9 unlockable achievement badges. Authentication is handled through a custom user model with email as the primary identifier, complete with email verification, password recovery, and CSP header enforcement in production. Code snippets are rendered with Prism.js syntax highlighting, and the interface supports both dark and light themes with persistent user preferences.
features: 3-Step AI Pipeline (Intent Parsing, Generation, Explanations)
Context-Aware Mistake Analysis and Guided Explanations
Gamification System (XP, Levels, Streaks, 9 Badges)
HTMX & Alpine.js SPA-like Interactive UI
Service-Oriented Django Architecture with Modular Apps
Email Verification, Password Recovery & CSP Enforcement
installation:
# Clone repository
git clone https://github.com/qtremors/quizzer-ai.git
cd quizzer-ai

# Setup environment
cp .env.example .env
# Add your GEMINI_API_KEY to .env

# Enter project folder and install dependencies
cd qtrmrs
uv sync

# Run migrations and start server
uv run python manage.py migrate
uv run python manage.py runserver

architecture.description: The system follows a Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA) where the AI orchestration logic is strictly decoupled from the web delivery layer. This ensures that the generative pipeline can be scaled or swapped (e.g., from Gemini to a self-hosted LLM) without affecting the core gamification or user management services.
decisions: Service Isolation Layer: Decouples AI prompt engineering and Gemini client execution inside apps/ai_agent/services.py, isolating generative logic from the web delivery layer.
HTMX-First Interactivity: Utilizes HTMX and Alpine.js for page updates and interactive quiz gameplay, achieving SPA-like responsiveness without frontend build tools or framework overhead.
Structured JSON Prompt Enforcement: Implements structured prompts with strict schema validation to ensure generated quiz questions, options, and explanations parse cleanly in a single pass.
Custom Auth & Profile Binding: Implements a custom Django user model using email as the primary identifier, bound 1:1 with user profiles for streaks, XP, leveling, and badges.

Dynamic Database Model Sync: Features custom manage.py commands (check_ai_config, sync_models, set_active_models) to fetch models from the Google Generative AI API and manage active defaults via database configurations.
architecture.scalability: Designed for horizontal scaling via stateless web workers. The AI pipeline uses asynchronous processing to prevent request-response blocking during long-running LLM calls.

title: Algorithm Visualizer
description: A real-time algorithm education platform that runs sorting and pathfinding algorithms on a FastAPI backend, then streams each execution step to a React visual workspace over WebSockets.
longDescription:
AlgoVisualizer is a full-stack visualization platform built with React 19, TypeScript, Vite, TailwindCSS, Python, and FastAPI. Algorithms are implemented from scratch on the backend as generator-driven classes, yielding structured execution steps that are streamed to the frontend through a persistent WebSocket connection instead of relying on pre-baked browser animations.

The platform supports Bubble Sort, Insertion Sort, and Selection Sort alongside Dijkstra, BFS, and DFS pathfinding algorithms. Pathfinding can be explored through editable 2D grids or weighted node-link graphs, with tools for drawing walls, moving start/end nodes, adding graph nodes, connecting weighted edges, deleting elements, generating random mazes, and adjusting graph zoom. The playback layer includes play, pause, step forward/back, reset, variable speed controls, estimated remaining time, synchronized pseudocode highlighting, algorithm complexity modals, and a scrolling execution log.
features: Real-Time FastAPI WebSocket Step Streaming
Bubble Sort, Selection Sort, Insertion Sort, BFS, DFS, and Dijkstra
Editable Grid Pathfinding with Walls, Start/End Nodes, and Random Mazes
Weighted Graph Builder with Node, Edge, Delete, Start, and End Tools
Playback Controls with Step Navigation, Speed Tuning, and Keyboard Shortcuts
Pseudocode Highlighting, Complexity Modals, and Execution Logs
installation:
# Clone repository
git clone https://github.com/qtremors/algorithm-visualizer.git
cd algorithm-visualizer

# Install dependencies
cd backend && uv sync && cd ..
cd frontend && npm install && cd ..

# Terminal 1: Backend
cd backend && uv run uvicorn app.main:api --reload

# Terminal 2: Frontend
cd frontend && npm run dev

architecture.description: A client-server architecture where the FastAPI backend owns algorithm execution and the React frontend focuses on interactive input, playback state, and visualization rendering.
decisions: Generator-Based Execution: Backend algorithms yield one structured step at a time, keeping algorithm logic inspectable while enabling live visualization.
Persistent WebSockets: Selected over REST polling so sorting, grid pathfinding, and graph pathfinding can stream compare, swap, visit, update, and path-found events in order.

Metadata-Driven UI: Each backend algorithm exposes pseudocode, complexity, descriptions, input type, and visualizer metadata so the frontend can render the right controls and educational context dynamically.
architecture.scalability: The backend uses FastAPI's asynchronous WebSocket handling while recent frontend and backend optimizations reduce unnecessary copying and re-rendering during large step sequences.

title: GitNexus
description: A local-first infrastructure companion for version control. Browse user profiles, track release assets, and time-travel through commit history with isolated dev environments powered by Git worktrees.
longDescription:
GitNexus is a privacy-centric developer tool built with a decoupled management UI and an asynchronous backend service, using SQLite with Fernet symmetric encryption for securely persisting API tokens and sensitive environment variables locally.

The Repo Replay module clones repositories, syncs their full commit history, and uses Git worktrees to browse the codebase at any point in time. Scoped environment variables (global, project, or commit-level) can be attached before spawning isolated HTTP dev servers for any commit. The Discovery Engine fetches GitHub user profiles, renders contribution graphs, and supports multi-repo bulk downloads. The Asset Watchtower monitors tracked repositories for new releases and enables direct asset downloads.
features: Repo Replay: Browse Commit History via Git Worktrees
Isolated HTTP Dev Servers per Commit State
Asset Watchtower: GitHub Release Tracking & Downloads
Discovery Engine: User Profiles & Bulk Repo Downloads
Fernet Symmetric Encryption for Tokens & Env Vars
Decoupled Async Architecture (React SPA + FastAPI)

cd backend && uv sync && cd ..

# Terminal 2: Frontend
cd frontend && npm run dev

architecture.description: A local-first, privacy-centric architecture that treats the user's machine as the primary compute node. It leverages a sidecar-style relationship between a secure Python backend and a web-based management UI.
decisions: Decoupled Client-Server Architecture: Connects a React 19 + Vite single page application with an asynchronous FastAPI backend via a typed REST API.
Git Worktree Manager: Utilizes zero-copy Git worktrees to allow developers to browse and run multiple code states simultaneously without disk duplication.
Fernet Symmetric Encryption: Protects local configuration settings, personal access tokens (PATs), and scoped environment variables (global, project, commit-level) at rest.
Asynchronous SQLite: Uses SQLAlchemy Async ORM and aiosqlite for zero-configuration, concurrent database persistence on the local filesystem.
Safe Path Traversal Guards: Implements structural blocklists and is_safe_path() checks to protect the local environment from directory traversal or system commands execution.
architecture.scalability: Scalability is handled via local process isolation; each 'Dev Server' spawned for a commit runs as an independent process, ensuring system stability even if a project crashes.

title: Arcile
description: A private Android file manager built with Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, and Material 3 Expressive, featuring multi-volume browsing, local-only storage analytics, Trash recovery, archives, and foreground file operations.
longDescription:
Arcile is a source-available Android file manager built for Android 11+ with Kotlin 2.2, Jetpack Compose, Material 3 Expressive, Hilt, StateFlow, typed Navigation Compose routes, and DataStore-backed preferences. It does not request the INTERNET permission, so browsing, indexing, thumbnails, archive handling, preferences, and file operations remain local to the device.

The app supports internal storage, SD-style volumes, and USB OTG-style temporary volumes with user-controlled classification. Its file-management surface includes a Home dashboard, volume-aware storage summaries, category shortcuts, recent files, quick access pins, advanced search filters, list/grid presentation controls, selection properties, safe open/share handoffs, and a storage dashboard with a Filelight-inspired radial Usage Map. Mutations run through foreground operation plumbing for copy, move, archive, extract, fake-file generation, Trash, and delete flows, with progress events, cancellation, conflict resolution, mutation recovery, and a lightweight operation journal. Arcile also includes a metadata-backed Trash system, conservative Storage Cleaner, ZIP/7z archive create/browse/extract workflows, custom Coil thumbnail fetchers for APK/audio/PDF/video content, onboarding for All Files Access, and extensive JVM/Robolectric plus instrumented test coverage.
features: Multi-Volume Browser for Internal, SD-Style, and USB OTG Storage
Home Dashboard, Recent Files, Quick Access, and Category Browsing
Storage Dashboard with Trash Visibility and Radial Usage Map
Foreground Copy, Move, Archive, Extract, Trash, Delete, and Fake-File Operations
Smart Paste Conflict Resolution and Metadata-Backed Trash Restoration
ZIP/7z Archive Workflows, Storage Cleaner, and Custom Media Thumbnails
installation:
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/qtremors/arcile.git

# Open in Android Studio
# File → Open → select the arcile-app directory

# Or build from the command line:
cd arcile/arcile-app
./gradlew assembleDebug

architecture.description: A single-module native Android app with package-level boundaries, MVVM ViewModels, repository/data-source separation, Hilt dependency injection, and StateFlow-backed Compose UI.
decisions: Offline-First Privacy: The Android manifest omits INTERNET permission, keeping file browsing, indexing, thumbnails, archive handling, and preferences on-device.
Repository Facade: LocalFileRepository coordinates volume discovery, MediaStore queries, filesystem mutations, folder stats, Trash, archives, and mutation finalization behind domain contracts.
Foreground Operation Pipeline: Long-running file mutations are routed through a coordinator/service pair with progress events, cancellation, conflict preflight, and journal-backed recovery.
architecture.scalability: Arcile is structured for modular growth, with feature-scoped ViewModels, typed routes, reusable delegates, injected dispatchers, and focused data managers for Trash, archives, storage usage, thumbnails, and operations. The architecture is prepared for a multi-module split so browser, storage, archive, cleaner, and shared core layers can evolve independently.

title: Arcade Nexus
description: A local arcade console for the browser with React, FastAPI, async SQLite persistence, local profiles, achievements, save slots, and a custom TypeScript Game SDK for Canvas and Three.js games.
longDescription:
Arcade Nexus is a full-stack, offline-capable arcade console built with React 19, TypeScript, Vite, TailwindCSS, Zustand, Framer Motion, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2, async SQLite, and Pydantic. The frontend provides a premium console-style interface with profile selection, a dashboard, store, library, achievements, settings, fullscreen gameplay, and a session-aware boot sequence.

The platform includes a typed Game SDK that separates game code from the console shell. Games implement a consistent lifecycle for initialization, frame updates, rendering, pause/resume, game over handling, score reporting, and optional save/load state. The current catalog includes Neon Snake and Raptor Run, with Stellar Flight represented as a Three.js flight simulation entry. Backend APIs manage local profiles, game metadata, user libraries, play statistics, detailed session history, high scores, achievements, and up to five save slots per game.
features: React 19 Premium Console UI with Boot, Dashboard, Store, Library, and Profile Flows
Typed TypeScript Game SDK for Canvas 2D and Three.js Game Instances
FastAPI REST Backend with SQLAlchemy 2, Pydantic, and Async SQLite
Local Profiles, Game Library, High Scores, Playtime, and Session History
Achievement Unlocks and Five Save Slots per Game
Keyboard/Gamepad Input, Fullscreen Play, and Offline Local Assets

architecture.description: A local client-server arcade shell where the React frontend hosts the console UI and game runtime while the FastAPI backend persists profiles, game catalog data, stats, saves, and achievements in SQLite.
decisions: Game SDK Pattern: Games implement shared lifecycle interfaces so the platform can run Canvas 2D and Three.js games through one engine, input layer, and fullscreen player.
Async SQLite Backend: Selected for a local-first arcade experience that persists progress without requiring a separate database server or cloud account.
Smart Game Sync: Seed data updates game metadata and achievements while preserving user progress, saves, stats, and unlocked achievements.
architecture.scalability: The modular frontend separates pages, stores, SDK primitives, and game implementations, while backend routers isolate profiles, games, library, stats, saves, and achievements for straightforward expansion with new games or persistence features.

title: Tremors Music
description: A local-first music player available as both a web application and a native Tauri desktop app. Features a Python FastAPI backend for metadata extraction and audio streaming, a React frontend with virtualized lists, and an Apple Music-inspired UI.
longDescription:
Tremors Music is a privacy-focused music player that runs as a web app or a native desktop application. The Python FastAPI backend handles ID3 metadata parsing via Mutagen, library scanning, and range-based audio streaming, while the React frontend provides virtualized lists for handling libraries of 10,000+ songs, synchronized LRC lyrics display, and smart playlists.

The desktop version uses Tauri with the Python backend compiled as a sidecar process, achieving a ~100-200MB RAM footprint compared to ~700-900MB in a browser tab. The application supports MP3, FLAC, M4A, WAV, OGG, WMA, AAC, and ALAC formats. All music data stays locally on the user's machine with no cloud dependencies.
features: Native Desktop App via Tauri with Python Sidecar
Virtualized Lists for 10,000+ Song Libraries
Synchronized LRC Lyrics & ID3 Metadata Extraction
SQLite Database with Smart Playlists
Range-Based Audio Streaming & Multi-Format Support
~100-200MB Desktop Memory Footprint

architecture.description: A native desktop app packaged via Tauri, using a Python FastAPI sidecar backend to scan media files, manage SQLite persistence, and stream audio ranges, while a React frontend handles UI rendering and queue playback.
decisions: Python Sidecar Pattern: Offloads metadata scanning (via Mutagen) and range-based audio streaming to an independent local Python service, reducing memory usage by ~70% compared to standard browser execution.
Virtualized List Rendering: Implements windowed list rendering for handling large libraries (10,000+ songs) smoothly without DOM bottlenecking.
Local SQLite Database: Synchronizes scanned track data and playlists locally using SQLModel, avoiding external database dependencies or cloud calls.
Sync-LRC Lyrics Renderer: Parses and renders embedded or external LRC files completely offline, synchronizing visual cues with audio playback time updates.
architecture.scalability: Decoupling player UI from the filesystem scanner via HTTP endpoints ensures the UI remains responsive during background scans, allowing horizontal expansion to other desktop platforms.

title: Xcrape
description: An asynchronous Python web scraper powered by Playwright and BeautifulSoup4. Extracts structured data, detects 20+ technologies, captures screenshots, and archives results to SQLite all through a Material Design 3 terminal-themed UI.
longDescription:
Xcrape is a locally-hosted web scraping tool built with FastAPI that uses headless Chromium via Playwright for JavaScript-rendered page extraction. It parses pages using BeautifulSoup4 to extract meta tags, headings, links, tables, images, JSON-LD, OpenGraph metadata, and social media profiles. A technology detection module fingerprints 20+ frameworks and CMS platforms.

Each scrape job captures a JPEG screenshot and archives all extracted data to a local SQLite database via aiosqlite. Users can filter historical jobs, trigger one-click re-scrapes, download scraped images individually or as bulk ZIP archives, and export results in CSV or JSON formats. The interface uses a terminal-themed Material Design 3 aesthetic with JetBrains Mono typography.
features: Playwright Engine with BeautifulSoup4 Parsing
Material Design 3 Terminal UI with JetBrains Mono
Technology Detection for 20+ Frameworks & CMS
Structured Data Extraction (JSON-LD, OpenGraph, Meta)
JPEG Screenshot Capture & Bulk Image Downloads
SQLite Archival with CSV/JSON Report Export
installation:

git clone https://github.com/qtremors/xcrape.git
cd xcrape/xcrape

# Install dependencies
uv sync

# Run the project
uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload

architecture.description: A modern monolithic scraping service featuring a FastAPI backend orchestration layer that spawns threaded workers for Playwright browser automation and SQLite persistence, coupled with a Jinja2-templated Material Design 3 frontend.
decisions: Threaded Playwright Workers: Executes scraping tasks in isolated background threads to prevent conflicts with the asyncio event loop in Windows environments.
Two-Stage Extraction Pipeline: Combines Playwright (Chromium) for JavaScript execution and rendering, with BeautifulSoup4 for fast, reliable HTML tag parsing.
Non-Blocking SQLite Storage: Persists scraping jobs, technology signatures, and metadata asynchronously using aiosqlite to avoid blocking the main server threads.
Inline Base64 Screenshots: Encodes captured JPEG screenshots directly into the SQLite database to eliminate the complexity of external file server hosting.
Jinja2 & Material Design 3 UI: Serves dynamic components directly from the server using Jinja2 templates and vanilla CSS/JS, keeping the visual presentation aligned with Material Design 3 standards.
architecture.scalability: By running scrapers on background threads and interacting asynchronously with SQLite, the system handles concurrent scrape tasks without blocking the user dashboard query interface.

title: Cosmos
description: A browser-based 3D space exploration simulator built with Three.js and React. Features a Solar System with 2K NASA textures, a secondary Quantumania dimension with 38 lazy-loaded 3D models, custom GLSL shaders, and 6-DOF flight controls with gamepad support.
longDescription:
Cosmos is a WebGL-based 3D universe exploration engine built with Three.js, React, and TypeScript. It features a multi-system architecture with a Solar System and a secondary Quantumania realm, navigated through 6-DOF flight controls with progressive boost mechanics and full gamepad support.

The Solar System contains 9 planets with 2K NASA textures, 4 moons, 2,000 instanced asteroid meshes, and a GLSL raymarched black hole. A radar minimap enables teleportation to the Quantumania dimension, which contains 38 lazy-loaded GLB models including floating mountains, structures, and the Arishem celestial entity with interior multi-point lighting. Custom GLSL shaders handle sun granulation, Earth day/night cycles, and atmospheric glow effects. A centralized physics SDK manages orbital mechanics with Kepler-based calculations.
features: Multi-System Architecture (Solar System + Quantumania)
6-DOF Flight Controls with Keyboard, Mouse, and Gamepad Support
2,000 Instanced Asteroids & 2K NASA Planet Textures
Custom GLSL Shaders (Sun Granulation, Earth Cycle, Raymarched Black Hole)
38 Lazy-Loaded GLB Models in Quantumania
Arishem (The Architect) Titan-Scale Celestial Entity with Interior Details
Radar Minimap with Entity Tracking & Teleportation
Cosmic Easter Eggs (The Kyln Nova Corps Prison, Explorer-1, Alien X)
installation:
# Clone repository
git clone https://github.com/qtremors/cosmos.git
cd cosmos/cosmos-app

# Install dependencies and run
npm install
npm run dev

architecture.description: A Component-Based 3D Architecture where the React UI controls the simulation overlay, the Three.js Scene manages WebGL rendering layers, and the Core SDK executes underlying physics, input handling, and orbital calculations.
decisions: Centralized SDK: All physics constants, Kepler-based calculations, and interpolation helpers are consolidated in a single module to enforce consistency and decoupling.
Three.js Layers (0, 1, 2): Segmented rendering and lighting contexts (Solar vs. Quantumania vs. Shared objects) to maintain high performance and avoid light bleeding.
Asynchronous Lazy Loading: The 38+ GLB models (~53MB) for Quantumania are only fetched when the camera approaches or teleports to the system.
External GLSL Shaders: Modularized all inline custom WebGL shaders (accretion disk, planet atmospheres, day/night cycles) into external .glsl files for cleaner codebase structure.
architecture.scalability: Expanding the simulation to support new celestial bodies or extra star systems requires registering configuration in the SDK and loading them under the SystemManager singleton, without changing core scene rendering loops.

title: LocalGhost
description: A local-first security auditing and benchmarking toolkit for development servers. Runs 11 asynchronous scanners covering port discovery, security headers, SSL/TLS analysis, CORS auditing, load testing, and DDoS resilience with weighted scoring and report exports.
longDescription:
LocalGhost is a Python-based security auditing CLI tool built with FastAPI, designed for hardening local development environments. It executes 11 concurrent asynchronous scanners: port scanning with service identification across 35+ known services, vulnerability detection for 7 security headers and 18 sensitive file paths, SSL/TLS certificate and cipher suite analysis, CORS misconfiguration detection, cookie security auditing, technology fingerprinting, DNS enumeration, and XSS scanning.

Beyond security auditing, it performs configurable load testing with percentile latency metrics (p50/p95/p99) and DDoS resilience testing including connection flood and slowloris scenarios. Results are scored on a weighted 0-100 scale with letter grades (A+ through F) and category breakdowns. All scans are persisted to a local SQLite database for historical comparison, with JSON report export capability. The frontend uses a Material Design 3 dashboard built with Vanilla HTML, CSS, and ES Modules.
features: 11 Concurrent Asynchronous Security Scanners
Weighted 0-100 Scoring Engine with Letter Grades
Configurable Load Testing & DDoS Resilience Testing
Material Design 3 Dashboard (Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS)
SQLite Scan History with JSON Report Export
XSS Detection, CORS Audit & SSL/TLS Analysis
installation:
# Clone and navigate
git clone https://github.com/qtremors/localghost.git

# Run the project
uv run python -m backend.main

architecture.description: A multi-threaded scanning engine designed for high-concurrency auditing. The architecture prioritizes speed and non-blocking execution to provide instant feedback on complex security postures.
decisions: Asynchronous Execution: Executes all 11 scanner modules concurrently using Python's asyncio.gather, reducing total test times by 80%.
Routers-Services-Scanners Layers: Decouples REST route definitions, scan orchestration services, and individual scanner modules for easier unit testing.
Vanilla Frontend with ES Modules: Employs a zero-build client interface structured with ES Modules, eliminating webpack/vite compilation complexity.
Weighted Scoring (0–100): Implements a CVSS-inspired heuristic scoring algorithm with categories weighted by security impact to yield letter grades (A+ through F).
SQLite via aiosqlite: Persists scan reports on the local filesystem using async SQLite connections to maintain history without backend database servers.
architecture.scalability: The scanning engine is horizontally scalable; multiple scanning nodes can be deployed to audit large internal networks simultaneously, with centralized reporting via a shared SQLite/PostgreSQL instance.

title: Earnslate
description: A client-side finance tracking platform built with Next.js and TypeScript. Manage transactions, set budgets with auto-reset, and track subscriptions with treemap visualizations all persisted locally via browser storage.
longDescription:
Earnslate is a personal finance management application built entirely on Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript and CSS Modules. All data is persisted in the browser via Zustand with localStorage, ensuring financial data never leaves the user's device.

The dashboard renders real-time spending breakdowns with interactive pie and donut charts. A transaction ledger supports search, multi-variable filtering, date presets, pagination, and batch deletion. The budgeting system tracks progress per category and automatically resets on period expiry. A subscription manager includes 100+ pre-loaded service templates and uses treemap visualizations to show recurring cost distribution. Data can be exported and imported via CSV/JSON for backup and portability.
features: Client-Side Next.js App with Zustand State
100% LocalStorage Persistence (No Backend)
Monochrome UI with Dark/Light Mode Toggle
Budget Tracking with Automated Period Expiry
Transaction Ledger with Multi-Variable Filtering
Subscription Treemaps & CSV/JSON Data Export
installation:

git clone https://github.com/qtremors/earnslate.git
cd earnslate/earnslate-web

# Install dependencies and run
npm install
npm run dev

architecture.description: A client-side Single Page Application (SPA) architecture built with Next.js App Router and TypeScript, featuring complete local-first persistence via Zustand state synchronization with browser storage.
decisions: Zustand State Store: Utilized for lightweight, client-side global state management, integrating persistence middleware to synchronize states seamlessly with browser storage.
Zero-Backend Local-First Design: Keeps financial transactions, budget details, and subscription trackers entirely in the user's browser, prioritizing complete privacy and offline usability.
CSS Modules: Standardized component styling using isolated CSS Modules mapped to central HSL design tokens, avoiding styling side-effects or heavy framework overhead.
On-Demand Iconify Fetching: Integrates Lucide React and Iconify dynamically, enabling the lookup and rendering of 100+ custom brand subscription templates without inflating the initial bundle size.
architecture.scalability: Built with a modular folder layout dividing features into store domains and custom React hooks, allowing new financial visualizations (e.g., CSV imports/exports or Android companion interfaces) to be easily integrated.

title: Amanzon E-Commerce
description: A full-stack e-commerce platform built with Django and PostgreSQL (Supabase). Handles product catalogs, Razorpay payments, order lifecycle management, discount coupons, user reviews, and email-verified authentication.
longDescription:
Amanzon is a full-featured e-commerce application built on Django with a Supabase PostgreSQL database. It uses server-side rendering with Bootstrap for a responsive storefront interface with dark mode support.

The platform implements the complete purchase lifecycle: product browsing with category filtering and search, persistent cart and wishlist, multi-address management, discount coupon validation, and checkout via the Razorpay API with a demo mode for testing. Order management supports status tracking, cancellation, and refund processing. Authentication uses email-verified registration with OTP-based password recovery and rate limiting. Administrative features include product management, coupon creation, and order oversight through the Django admin panel.
features: Django + PostgreSQL (Supabase) Architecture
Razorpay Checkout with Demo Mode
Order Lifecycle (Status Tracking, Cancellation, Refunds)
Discount Coupon System with Usage Tracking
Email-Verified Auth with OTP Password Reset
Product Reviews, Multi-Address Management & Dark Mode

architecture.description: A full-stack monolithic architecture built with Django, designed for ACID-compliant transactional integrity. The system leverages a robust relational schema to manage complex order lifecycles and payment states.
decisions: PostgreSQL (Supabase): Chosen for reliable relational data management and advanced querying capabilities required for product filtering and analytics.
Razorpay Webhook Integration: Implemented an idempotent processing layer to handle payment confirmations and prevent duplicate order fulfillment.
Django Signals: Utilized for decoupled post-save actions like automated email notifications and inventory adjustments.
architecture.scalability: Scalability is achieved through database indexing and session-based caching. The system is prepared for migration to a microservices architecture by maintaining strict service boundaries within the Django app structure.

title: Social Network Platform
description: A frontend prototype of a social networking platform built with React, Tailwind CSS, and Zustand. Features public feeds, direct messaging, community channels, user profiles, and a dual-mode navigation sidebar.
longDescription:
SocNet is a frontend prototype that combines public broadcast feeds and community-based channel spaces within a unified interface. Users can compose posts, interact through likes and replies, engage in direct and group messaging, and discover trending topics and communities.

Built with React, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS, the application uses Zustand for client-side state management with simulated mock data. A dual-mode navigation sidebar contextually switches between global navigation and community channel lists depending on the active route. Community spaces support text and voice channels. The interface includes user profiles, notification center, settings panel, and an explore page.
features: Dual-Mode Navigation Sidebar (Global & Community)
Public Feed with Posts, Likes, Replies & Reposts
Direct & Group Messaging Interface
Community Spaces with Text & Voice Channels
User Profiles, Notifications & Settings
React + Vite + Tailwind CSS + Zustand

title: Material Design
description: A zero-dependency implementation of Material Design 3, Material You, and Material 3 Expressive specifications in pure HTML, CSS custom properties, and vanilla JavaScript.
longDescription:
This project recreates Google's Material Design 3 component system entirely with vanilla web technologies and no build tools or framework dependencies. It uses CSS custom properties for theming, with a dynamic color engine supporting light/dark modes and multiple color seed palettes.

The implementation includes Buttons, Cards, Input fields, Dialogs, Bottom Sheets, Chips, and responsive Navigation components (Rail and Drawer), all injected dynamically via JavaScript. A custom ripple effect system replicates the material interaction pattern natively. An interactive playground page exposes all 300+ generated design tokens for real-time inspection and testing.
features: Zero Dependencies (No Build Tools or Frameworks)
Dynamic Light/Dark Mode & Color Seed Generation
Custom JavaScript Ripple Effect System
MD3 Components (Buttons, Cards, Dialogs, Sheets, Chips)
Responsive Navigation Rail & Drawer
Developer Playground with 300+ CSS Design Tokens
installation:
# Clone repository
git clone https://github.com/qtremors/material-design.git
cd material-design

architecture.description: A static build-free component workbench implementing the Google Material Design 3, Material You, and Material 3 Expressive specifications. It relies on standard browser APIs, vanilla JavaScript, and native CSS custom properties.
decisions: Zero-Dependency Pipeline: Avoids compilers, bundlers, and package dependencies entirely, running directly on raw browser technologies for optimal loading speeds.
CSS Variables Token System: Declares 300+ design tokens inside variables.css (colors, type, elevations) to control dynamic theming and color seeds.
Global Event Delegation: Attaches click listeners at the document level in interactions.js to capture and orchestrate clicks based on custom data-action attributes.
HTML Seed Attribute: Applies theme attributes (data-theme, data-seed) directly to the html node, letting CSS variables adapt colors in real-time.
Custom Ripple Animation: Standardizes component focus-states by calculating click offsets and rendering ink ripples dynamically via JavaScript.
architecture.scalability: New components or widgets are easily integrated by linking their modular CSS, writing standard semantic HTML, and registering them under the navigation.js collection without compilation.

title: ReConText
description: A statically generated knowledge base for developer cheat sheets and research notes. Built with Next.js and MDX, featuring auto-inferred metadata, interactive React components within markdown, and a dark "Cosmic Night" theme.
longDescription:
ReConText is a static knowledge management site built on Next.js with MDX content support via next-mdx-remote and rehype-pretty-code for syntax highlighting. Content files are dropped into a directory structure and processed with auto-inferred titles, dates, difficulty levels, and reading time estimates.

The platform supports MDX, allowing embedded React components such as tabbed code blocks and alert callouts within standard markdown documents. Navigation is handled through auto-generated breadcrumb trails and dynamically rendered Tables of Contents. The interface uses a "Cosmic Night" dark theme with glassmorphism accents and Framer Motion page transitions. The site is fully responsive and statically generated for fast load times.
features: MDX Content with Embedded React Components
Auto-Inferred Metadata (Title, Date, Difficulty, Reading Time)
Auto-Generated Table of Contents & Breadcrumbs
Static Site Generation via Next.js App Router
Cosmic Night Dark Theme with Framer Motion Transitions
Responsive Layout for Mobile, Tablet & Desktop

title: Diffs
description: A local-first browser-based text and image comparison platform built with Next.js and React. Features character-level text diffing, pixel-level image comparisons with overlay slider, zoom and pan controls, and IndexedDB local persistence.
longDescription:
Diffs is a local-first comparison workbench built on Next.js and React that executes all diff calculations directly inside the user's browser, ensuring sensitive code and assets never leave the machine. The platform features a plugin-style comparison engine that routes files by format, supporting both text and image comparison.

For text, it implements character-level intra-line highlighting using jsdiff and synchronized side-by-side scrolling. For images, it offers four comparison modes (side-by-side, overlay slider, pixel-level difference detection via pixelmatch, and raw metadata comparison) with mouse-scroll zooming (1x–8x) and drag-to-pan. Uploaded files are persisted locally using IndexedDB to survive page reloads. The interface uses a clean monochrome design with colors reserved strictly for highlighting differences.
features: Character-Level Text Diffing & Synchronized Scrolling
Image Comparison (Side-by-Side, Overlay Slider, and Pixel Diff)
IndexedDB Local Browser Persistence for Uploaded Files
Scroll-to-Zoom (1x-8x) & Drag-to-Pan on Image Views
Multi-File Comparison with Dynamic Original Selection
Monochrome UI with High-Contrast Diff Accents
installation:

architecture.description: A client-side modular comparison workbench built using Next.js App Router and TypeScript. The architecture decouples the state manager hook from the pluggable comparison engine, which routes files based on MIME types.
decisions: Client-Side Execution: All text and image comparison calculations run entirely in the browser to ensure absolute privacy and security of files.
Pluggable Diff Engine: Comparison algorithms (jsdiff for text, pixelmatch for images) are dispatched dynamically by file format for modular scaling.
IndexedDB Local Storage: Uses browser-side storage to persist uploads across page reloads without requiring an external database or backend server.
Scroll-to-Zoom & Pan Hooks: Leverages custom event hooks to control zooming (1x-8x) and panning on image elements within the comparison viewport.
architecture.scalability: Adding new file comparison types (e.g., CSV, JSON, or PDF) only requires registering a new file parser and renderer under the comparison engine, leaving core app layout and state hooks unchanged.

title: GTRMRS
description: A unified suite of dependency-free, Git-aware Python CLI tools. Includes rtree (directory tree visualization), locr (lines-of-code counting with language breakdown), and gitmig (clean repository migration).
longDescription:
GTRMRS is a Python CLI toolchain that bundles three development utilities into a single installable package with zero third-party dependencies. It uses only the standard library, ensuring cross-platform compatibility.

The suite includes: rtree, which generates plain-text ASCII directory trees with configurable depth and automatic .gitignore-aware pruning; locr, which counts lines of code per file with language identification, percentage breakdowns, and JSON output; and gitmig, which copies repository directories while stripping .git history, node_modules, and virtual environments, with support for dry-run previews and ZIP archival.
features: Zero Dependencies (Python Standard Library Only)
Git-Aware with Automatic .gitignore Pruning
rtree: ASCII Directory Tree Visualization
locr: Lines of Code Counting with Language Breakdown
gitmig: Repository Copy with Bloat Stripping
Cross-Platform (Windows, macOS, Linux)
installation:
# Clone and install
git clone https://github.com/qtremors/gtrmrs.git
cd gtrmrs
pip install -e .

# Usage
rtree
locr
gitmig ./backup --dry-run

architecture.description: A unified CLI toolchain built entirely on the Python 3.8+ Standard Library, combining three Git-aware utilities using shared core configurations for color styling, exclusion patterns, and scanning logic.
decisions: Zero-Dependency Footprint: Relies exclusively on standard library modules (like argparse, subprocess, os, fnmatch) to ensure instant, lightweight installation on any platform.

2-Phase Hybrid Scanning: Uses Phase 1 Eager Pruning to skip heavy folders (node_modules, venv, .git) before walking them, combined with Phase 2 Git precision (git check-ignore) for 100% accurate scans.
Subcommand Router Pattern: Implements an argparse subparsers mapping to route commands (rtree, locr, gitmig) to their respective core engines dynamically.
Git-Aware Utility Core: Centralizes repository status checks and ignore evaluations in a single shared git_utils library for all subcommands.
architecture.scalability: New command-line utilities can be added by dropping a package directory into gtrmrs/ containing an engine and argument parser, then registering the subparser in cli.py, without modifying existing tools.

title: Plant Disease Detector
description: A Django web application that uses TensorFlow and a fine-tuned MobileNetV2 model to classify apple leaf diseases from uploaded images. Renders prediction confidence via Plotly.js charts and persists scan history in SQLite.
longDescription:
This application demonstrates deploying a deep learning image classification model within a Django web framework. A MobileNetV2 convolutional neural network, pre-trained on ImageNet and fine-tuned via transfer learning on the PlantVillage dataset, classifies apple leaf images into four categories: Apple Scab, Black Rot, Cedar Apple Rust, and Healthy.

The interface provides a drag-and-drop image upload zone built with Bootstrap. Uploaded images are processed through the TensorFlow inference pipeline, and prediction probabilities are rendered as interactive charts via Plotly.js. All scans are automatically saved to a local SQLite database for historical reference. The model is scoped to apple leaves only and is designed as an educational proof of concept.
features: Fine-Tuned MobileNetV2 Transfer Learning Model
TensorFlow Inference for 4 Apple Leaf Classes
Interactive Plotly.js Probability Charts
Drag-and-Drop Image Upload (Bootstrap)
SQLite Scan History with Past Results
Django + Python Backend

title: PC Remote Control
description: A Python FastAPI server that turns any mobile browser into a remote control for a desktop workstation. Supports media playback, volume control, system power operations, remote screenshots, and browser launching all over the local network.
longDescription:
PC Remote Control runs a lightweight FastAPI server on the desktop that serves a vanilla HTML/JS mobile interface accessible from any device on the same Wi-Fi network. It uses PyAutoGUI for simulating keyboard inputs and MSS for screen capture.

The mobile interface provides media playback controls (play/pause, volume, track navigation), system power operations (lock, sleep, reboot, shutdown), and a remote screenshot feature that captures the desktop screen and serves it as a compressed JPEG to the mobile display. A browser launcher button can open the default web browser on the PC remotely. The application runs with minimal resource overhead (~40-60MB RAM).
features: FastAPI Local Network Control Server
Vanilla HTML/JS Mobile Web Interface
Media Playback & Volume Control via PyAutoGUI
System Power Operations (Sleep, Lock, Reboot, Shutdown)
Remote Desktop Screenshot Capture via MSS
Cross-Platform Support (Windows, macOS, Linux)

title: Tremors
description: A multi-mode personal portfolio website built with Next.js. Features 5 distinct viewing modes (Cards, Terminal, AI Newspaper, Resume, Nexus Space), GitHub integration, AI-generated content via Google Gemini, and a fully functional interactive CLI.
longDescription:
Tremors is a personal portfolio application built on Next.js with React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Framer Motion. It offers five distinct viewing modes: a modern card grid (Default), an interactive CLI terminal with 30+ commands (Terminal), an AI-generated newspaper mode (Newspaper), a professional resume view (Paper), and a 3D space landing (Nexus).

The Newspaper mode uses the Google Gemini Flash API with a "Skye" news agent that generates content in 4 distinct personalities (Tabloid, Senior, Scholar, Hacker) based on real GitHub activity. A PostgreSQL database managed by Prisma ORM stores project metadata, cached GitHub API data, and admin sessions. A hidden admin interface accessible through the Terminal mode provides CMS-style controls for managing project visibility, feature flags, and content editing with HMAC-signed authentication.
features: 5 Viewing Modes (Cards, Terminal, Newspaper, Resume, Nexus)
Interactive Terminal with 30+ Commands & Autocomplete
AI Content Generation via Google Gemini (4 Personalities)
GitHub Integration for Repository Stats & Activity
Hidden Admin CMS with HMAC-Signed Authentication
PostgreSQL + Prisma ORM Backend

npx prisma db push

architecture.description: A full-stack web portfolio built with Next.js App Router, using React Server Components for fast data fetching and Client Components for dynamic 3D elements and interactive terminal CLI utilities, with Prisma ORM connecting to a PostgreSQL instance.
decisions: React Server Components (RSC): Uses RSCs to query repository statistics and cached GitHub activity directly on the server, eliminating frontend API fetch cycles.
Decoupled Skye Agent: Runs a Google Gemini Flash agent in background API routes to parse real GitHub commit activity logs and author news articles with 4 selectable personalities.
Prisma Database Indexes: Defines database indices on Repo (featured, hidden) and Newspaper/Activity (date) fields within PostgreSQL (Neon) to speed up filtering and content queries.
Custom HMAC-Signed Admin Auth: Implements secure admin cookie verification using PBKDF2 and HMAC-SHA256, protecting CMS route handlers from CSRF and cross-origin traversal attacks.
Edge-Runtime Rate Limiting: Employs Next.js Edge Middleware to intercept incoming requests and apply rate limits on authentication and AI generation endpoints before triggering backend code.
architecture.scalability: Stateless Next.js deployment models allow scaling the web application horizontally, while rate limits and database index tuning maintain high efficiency even during sudden traffic spikes.

title: The Scrapyard
description: A cyberpunk-themed digital archive for abandoned and unfinished web projects. Built with a custom Node.js static site generator that scans project directories and compiles HTML pages with live preview iframes and canvas-based digital rain.
longDescription:
The Scrapyard is an interactive digital archive that showcases abandoned and scrapped web project prototypes in a cyberpunk-themed interface. A custom Node.js build script scans a projects directory, reads metadata, and compiles static HTML pages with template injection.

The interface features terminal-style search filtering, live preview iframes triggered on card hover, and a throttled HTML5 Canvas digital rain background animation. Projects are organized into categories (Portfolio, Games, 3D Models, Components, Demos) with color-coded visual indicators. The site is deployed via GitHub Actions to GitHub Pages.
features: Custom Node.js Static Site Generator
HTML5 Canvas Digital Rain Animation (30fps Throttled)
Terminal-Style Search Filtering
Live Preview Iframes on Card Hover
Cyberpunk UI with Glitch Effects & Neon Accents
Automated GitHub Pages Deployment

architecture.description: A static build-time compiled archive utilizing a custom Node.js static site generator to index local category paths and output a highly optimized, responsive single-page web environment containing interactive previews.
decisions: Vanilla JS & Zero Dependencies: Avoids bundlers, frameworks, and build transpilers to ensure long-term archival stability and resistance to framework deprecation.
Scattered to Grid Toggle: Implements a responsive layout that displays items in a scattered, chaotic theme by default, then contextually switches to a structured grid layout upon search interaction.
Debounced Background Previews: Restricts iframe instantiation for card previews with a 1-second debounce, preventing excessive browser resource utilization and network latency during mouse movement.
Throttled Canvas Frame-Rate: Caps the HTML5 Canvas matrix digital rain animation to a maximum of 30 frames per second, significantly reducing GPU utilization and power consumption.
Local metadata.json Catalogs: Aggregates subfolder discovery and custom file configuration (meta.json) into a centralized, queryable static index, speeding up site generation and browser searches.
architecture.scalability: Expanding the directory only requires adding standard HTML folders to categories; the Node.js compiler recursively indexes them without additional configuration, enabling static hosting directly on GitHub Pages.
